senses.gloss:
व्योकार व्यो-कार, अस्, m. (probably onoma-
topoetic), ‘making the sound व्यो,’ a blacksmith.

व्योमन् व्योमन्, अ, n. (according to Uṇā-
di-s. IV. 150. fr. rt. व्ये above; according to others
fr. ओ for अव् with वि, cf. ओमन्, or connected
with rt. 2. दिव्), sky, heaven, atmosphere, ether;
water; a temple sacred to the sun, a place where
the sun is especially worshipped; talc, mica; (आ),
m., N. of a king.
—व्योम-केश, अस्, or व्योम-
केशिन्, ई, m. ‘sky-haired,’ an epithet of Śiva.
—व्यो-
म-गङ्गा, f. the heavenly Ganges.
—व्योम-चर,
अस्, आ, अम्, ‘sky-going,’ passing through the air.
—व्योम-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, sky-going; (ई), m. ‘air-
goer,’ ‘sky-goer;’ a god; a bird; a saint; a
[]
Brāhman.
—व्योमचारि-पुर, अम्, n. ‘sky-floating
city,’ the city of Hari-ścandra (supposed to be sus-
pended between heaven and earth).
—व्योम-देव, अस्,
m., N. of Śiva
—व्योम-धूम, अस्, m. ‘sky-smoke,’
a cloud.
—व्योम-नासिका, f. a sort of quail.
—व्योम-
पञ्चक, अम्, n. an aggregate of five Vyomans (?) .
—व्योम-मञ्जर, अम्, n. ‘sky-cluster,’ a flag,
banner.
—व्योम-मण्डल, अम्, n. ‘sky-circle,’ a
flag, banner.
—व्योम-मध्ये, ind. in the middle
of the sky, in mid-air.
—व्योम-माय, अस्, आ, अम्,
‘sky-measuring,’ reaching to the sky, high as the
heaven.
—व्योम-मुद्गर, अस्, m. ‘sky-hammer,’
a gust of wind.
—व्योम-यान, अम्, n. ‘sky-vehicle,’
a celestial car, chariot of the gods.
—व्योम-वर्त्-
मन्, अ, n. the path of the sky, (व्योम-वर्त्मना,
inst. c. through the air or sky.)
—व्योम-विस्तृत,
अम्, n. the expanse of heaven, the sky, firmament.
—व्योम-सद्, त्, m. ‘sky-dweller,’ a deity, divinity;
a Gandharva; a spirit.
—व्योम-स्थली, f. ‘ground
or base of the sky,’ the earth.
—व्योम-स्पृश्, क्, क्,
क्, ‘sky-touching,’ ‘sky-reaching,’ lofty.
—व्योमाभ
(˚म-आभ), अस्, m. ‘heaven-like,’ a Buddha or a
Jaina deified saint.
—व्योमोदक (˚म-उद्˚), अम्,
n. ‘sky-water,’ rain-water, dew (= दिव्योदक).

व्योम्निक in परम-व्योम्निक, अस्, आ, अम्,
relating to the highest ether.

व्योष व्योष, अम्, n. (probably fr. rt. 1.
व्युष् or fr. rt. 1. उष् with वि), the aggregate of three
spices (black pepper, long pepper, and dry ginger).

व्य्-ओदन, Ved. having various kinds of grain or
food.
